template.summary: Advances the shared fold value by its signed delta, clamps it to 0..0x1000, clears active at an endpoint, and returns whether the tween is complete or inactive.
unknowns: A representative runtime capture is still needed to determine whether every module applies the fold primitive exclusively to windows.

template.signature: void tweenLinearStart(TweenLinear *self, int32_t start, int32_t end, int32_t duration)
template.summary: Starts a generic 8.8 fixed-point linear tween: seeds accum=start<<8 and delta=((end-start)<<8)/duration signed, sets active. Leaves the record untouched when start==end. Distinct from the window-fold tween: different struct, arbitrary range, no SFX.
unknowns: TweenLinear+0x04 is never read or written by either family member; its meaning is unknown.

No caller is known for any member, so what each tween animates on screen is not established.

template.summary: Ticks the generic 8.8 linear tween: returns 1 immediately when inactive, else advances accum by delta, sets current=accum>>8, clamps direction-aware against target, and on clamp snaps to target, clears active and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
unknowns: No caller is known for any member, so what each tween animates on screen is not established.

template.signature: void statusScreenEntryPopulate(StatusScreenRow *rows, int32_t index, int32_t visible)
template.summary: Fills in or blanks one block of the pause/status screen. With visible set, it looks the selected entry up through the shared record service, writes the entry's label into the block's title element, then walks five value elements and five icon elements, giving each its text and its position from a per-block layout table. With visible clear, it hides the title, the five values and the five icons instead. Each member differs only in which layout table it reads, so the copies are the different blocks of that screen.
evidence: parameterized homolog cluster: members differ only in one layout-table pointer (0x8009a784, 0x8009a830, 0x8009a8a4, 0x8009a93c, 0x8009a964)
both shape variants take the same three arguments and branch on the third
unknowns: The meanings of shared-object slots 0x114, 0x118, 0x144 and 0x148 are assumed to be set-content, set-content-indirect, set-visible and set-enabled from usage alone; none has been established from original assembly.
Which screen block each layout table drives has not been determined.
Whether the five value elements and five icon elements are fixed at five for every block, or the loop bound is table-driven, is not established.
The record service at 0x80048d34 slots 0x2718/0x2734/0x2750 is unidentified.

template.summary: Blocks until one of four kernel events fires. It spins on four flag words, and as soon as any is set it acknowledges all four events through the BIOS TestEvent call, clears the four flags, and returns which one fired. This is the stall the player sees as a brief pause while the game waits on the hardware.
evidence: TestEvent is a symbol of the original assembly, called four times inside this function's range at 0x8003e098, 0x8003e0a8, 0x8003e0b8 and 0x8003e0c8
the four flag words D0x800829d0/d4/d8/dc are written outside this function and only read and cleared inside it
unknowns: Which four kernel events these are has NOT been established. The obvious reading is the disc events, but no OpenEvent call site has been tied to these four flag words, so the subsystem is unconfirmed.
The returned value is the flag bitmask shifted right by one; whether callers treat it as an index or as a mask has not been checked.
The second member differs in one global address and has not been read separately.

template.summary: Every menu overlay builds its own root panel object this way: it asks the shared object factory for a 0x68-byte object of the overlay's own class, installs the overlay's per-frame callback at slot 0x64, sets slot 0x50 to 0x1000 and clears slot 0x54. 0x1000 is the same 12.4 fixed-point 1.0 the window-fold tween runs to, so slot 0x50 is most likely the panel's fully-open extent.
evidence: parameterized homolog cluster with nine members, one per UI overlay, differing only in the class pointer and the callback address
calls exe/fns:F0x80014504, which build_recovered_inventory.py already establishes as a shared object factory whose first argument is a literal callback/class address
the constant 0x1000 matches the endpoint of the curated window-fold tween family
unknowns: That slot 0x50 is an extent, and 0x54 a phase, is inferred from the shared 0x1000 constant alone and is NOT established.
The 0x68-byte layout has not been recovered beyond the three slots written here.
Whether slot 0x64 is a per-frame callback or a one-shot initialiser is unconfirmed.

template.signature: int16_t stageAnimStepCursor0(AnimCursor *cursor, const AnimScriptEntry *script, int32_t oneShot, int32_t depth)

template.signature: void stageAnimStepTable(StageActor *actor, const AnimEntry **table, AnimTableCursor *cursor, int32_t depth)
template.summary: Drives an actor from a table of animation sequences instead of one script. The cursor is {u16 sequence, u16 entry, s32 timer}; each 4-byte entry is {u8 frame, u8 hold, u8 second, u8 lastInSequence}. On timer expiry a non-zero lastInSequence advances the sequence and resets the entry, a null next pointer wraps the sequence index to 0, and the table therefore repeats forever. On the outermost call the entry's frame byte goes to actor +4 and its second byte to actor +9. 2 copies.

structure_fields.name: holdTimer
structure_fields.note: s32, unlike the halfword timer of the single-level forms

The four members differ only in the code (0x43, 0x46, 0x47, 0x4c).

template.summary: Builds a graphics-processor drawing-area command word. Clamps x against the halfword at 0x80055efc and y against 0x80055efe, forces a negative coordinate to zero, masks each to 10 bits and packs x in bits 0-9 and y in bits 10-19 under the command byte. The two members differ only in that byte: 0xE3 for the top-left corner, 0xE4 for the bottom-right.
unknowns: Where the two clamp limits are written is not established.

template.summary: Interpolates between two values over a duration. Reads an 8-byte table entry holding a duration at +0, an end value at +4 and a start value at +6, and returns start + (end - start) * elapsed / duration using the object's counter at +0x52. Once the counter reaches the duration it returns the end value, so the result never overshoots.

template.summary: A two-state tick that runs the object's own routine at +0x3c a fixed number of times with a pause between runs. State 2 waits until two frame counts have passed and returns to state 1.

template.summary: Another form of the per-stage animation-script stepper. On the reset band it calls the actor's +0x38 method and seeds its halfword cursor fields at +0x50..+0x5a from per-stage overlay halfwords. On state 1 it advances each cursor through the overlay's shared stepper primitive at 0x800a5de0, then walks the stride-0x12 record list held at 0x80099d90 and writes the stepped value into every record whose tag byte matches.
unknowns: What the stride-0x12 records at 0x80099d90 represent on screen, and what the tag byte means, are not established.
The per-stage script data each cursor walks was not read.

template.summary: Screen entry routine shared by nine screen overlays. On the entry state band it drives the resident display service at 0x8004de10: calls +0x150, then +0x154(0x5000), sets the full-frame extent 0x140 by 0xf0 through +0x174, builds a matching zero-origin rectangle and passes it to +0x16c(rect, 1, 0x1000), then calls +0x12c on the returned object. It stores a per-overlay value into the caller's out-parameter and finishes by calling the actor's own +0x38 method.
unknowns: What the display service methods do on the hardware is not established; only the call order, the service pointer and the full-frame extent are.
The value stored into the out-parameter comes from a per-overlay call that was not read.

template.signature: void fadeStartSignedStep(FadeState *fade, int32_t direction, int32_t duration)
template.summary: Starts a fade in either direction. Calls the object's +0x28 method with 1, sets +0x10 to 1 and +0x58 to the requested direction, then either stores start value 0 at +0x5c with step +(0xff00 / duration) at +0x60, or start value 0xff00 with the same step negated. Both directions share one divisor.

template.signature: void indexedTableRecordUpdate(int16_t a, int16_t b, int16_t c, void *rec, ...)
template.summary: Read-modify-write on one record of an indexed table. Opens with readIndexedTableRecord4, builds a small record on the stack from the trailing arguments, applies it through the helpers 0x80031a3c and 0x80031a98, and closes with writeIndexedTableRecord4 on the same three index arguments.
unknowns: Which table is indexed, and what the modified field means, are not established.

template.summary: Puts one class-addressed stage actor into a fixed mode and cues a sound while doing it. The routine asks the resident object registry (through the pointer at 0x8004b7bc) for the object of a single class -- 0x18 in wstag745, 0x19 in wstag746 -- with both index arguments -1. If that object exists and its state at +0x0c is not already the routine's mode, it plays packed sound 0x800410bd through the resident play-sound entry at 0x80055c48. It then calls the object's own +0x28 method with the mode and writes a literal into the object's +0x04. Three copies per overlay carry the modes (compare 1, argument 1, write 0), (2, 2, 0) and (1, 1, 1). In wstag745/746 the addressed object is the Dark Dungeon full-screen white wash; its +0x28 method is the default setPhase stub F0x80014274 and its +0x04 word is the wash's ramp trigger (0 = idle/off, 1 = ramp on).
unknowns: No caller of any of the six copies was traced (they are event-table native_fn entries).
What story moment selects the cue events in each Dark Dungeon room is not established.

template.summary: Reads the actor phase word at +0xC; when the phase is 0, negative, or 4 or greater, calls the actor's own +0x38 method. The 167 members are word-for-word the same 18-instruction routine, one per overlay, and the stage init that follows passes it as the first argument (the behaviour callback) to the actor factory (verified in wstag202 and wstag721).
unknowns: What sets the phase word at +0xC, what the per-actor +0x38 method does, and whether every member object is a stage actor rather than another first object.

template.summary: Per-stage entry-object tick and story-event trigger. When the phase word at +0xC is 0, negative or 4 or greater it first runs its own +0x38 method and then, when this stage's story conditions hold (the master ordinal at 0x8004B370 and/or one or two story-flag queries through 0x80048ACC), starts one scripted event through start_event at 0x800853F8 and stores the event-runner pointer in its extra buffer (+0/+4/+8). The event id and the ordinal/flag values are per-stage constants inside each body; 23 exact-body clusters, 45 members after the five members that have their own documented names, joined by the wstag212 copy read on 2026-09-11. What each event shows on screen is not established here.
unknowns: The event ids, ordinals and flag ids are per-stage data read from the bodies; what the events show is not established.
The clusters differ only in the condition/event layout; no word-identical match across clusters is claimed.

template.summary: Per-stage entry-object tick that both starts a story event and spawns child actors. On the phase-0/negative/>=4 band it calls its own +0x38 method and, under per-stage ordinal and flag conditions, starts one scripted event through start_event at 0x800853F8 and calls one or more of the stage's local constructors (F0x800143dc / F0x80014504 wrappers for the stage's effect and decor actors), storing the child pointers in its extra buffer next to the event-runner pointer. 12 exact-body clusters over 14 members, joined by the wstag310 and wstag311 controllers read on 2026-09-11; what each child draws is not established here.
unknowns: What each spawned child actor draws is not established; only the constructor call, size and class are read.
The event ids, ordinals and flag ids are per-stage data read from the bodies.

template.summary: One-shot stage-ambience bootstrap. On the phase-0/negative/>=4 band the entry object allocates the stage's animated ambient child through a local F0x80014504 / F0x800143dc wrapper (the child callback is the overlay's point-sprite decor stepper, usually 0x800a5ed4), stores the returned pointer in its extra buffer, and advances its own state; two of the members additionally bind the stage placement record first. The nine-row wstag232/233/481/555/630/645/730/731/949 cluster is the one confirmed at runtime to spawn the visible props; what each child draws is not established by this family.
unknowns: What each spawned child draws is not established; sprite ids are TMPK clip ids, not named art.
The dispatch route from stage choreography to these entry objects was not traced.

template.summary: Per-stage entry-object tick that binds the stage's placement record. On the phase-0/negative/>=4 band it calls the overlay's stage-record-bind routine with the story-step program pointer held at scene-descriptor +0x14, a per-stage record table address, and the two halfwords at 0x80048D34+0x44/+0x46, then calls its own +0x38 method. 32 members over three exact-body clusters; the routine it calls is the 34-copy stage-record-bind family.

What the per-stage table records represent is not established.

template.summary: Per-stage five-slot tagged-decor animator for wstag480/481. The sequence tables were not read.

template.summary: The wstag825/830 city-entry object constructor, replicated 16 times. It allocates a 0x54-byte object through F0x80014504 with the overlay's entry-gate callback 0x800a5ee4, stores the caller's argument at +0x50, and then calls the overlay's scene-setup routine through its per-overlay pointer global (0x800a5fac or 0x800a5fb4). The 16 bodies are one 23-word body; the seven F0x800a5f50 copies and the nine F0x800a5f58 copies differ only in the displacement of that pointer-global load.

template.summary: Two-slot prop animator: claims point records tagged 2 and 3 into its +0x50/+0x54 slot pointers, animates their sprite/palette fields each tick and moves a looked-up actor's position while playing sounds 0x8004103C / 0x01080001. wstag934 is word-identical to the wstag261 copy. What prop it drives is not established.

The two packed sounds are unidentified.

template.summary: Position/heading integrator for a moving prop. It accumulates the frame delta at +0x70 against +0x72, advances heading +0x76 through the sine/cosine helpers 0x8002abcc/0x8002ac9c times speed +0x74 into +0x64/+0x68, and derives tile coordinates at +0x6c/+0x6e with an arithmetic shift of 8. wstag526 is word-identical to the wstag460 copy.

template.signature: int32_t battleMemberChanceRoll(int32_t flag, int32_t memberIndex, int32_t unused)
template.summary: Chance check for a battle party member. When the first argument is zero and the global battle-active byte D0x80042b5b is set it returns 0; otherwise it sets two engine flags through F0x8009ec94, reads the member's stat byte at D0x80042bca+index*0x12+0xa, derives a threshold from it (shifted and divided by 8, clamped to 1..0x7f) and returns whether a random value (the function pointer at D0x8005dbf4) masked to 0x7f falls below that threshold. A player sees a member's action succeed or fail on a statistic-driven roll.
unknowns: The random source D0x8005dbf4 is a function pointer; the RNG algorithm is not read here.
The two engine flags set through F0x8009ec94 are not named.
Three members share this masked body and differ only in immediate arguments; the call sites are not identified.

template.summary: Resolves a battle actor object through the global accessor at D0x8005df90 (called with the object id), calls its virtual method at +0x150 with an engine table (0x80085110) and the actor pointer, then copies 32 bytes from the source struct into the actor record at +0x84 (two 4-word blocks). A player sees one fighter's stat/transform block transferred into its live battle record.
unknowns: The accessor at D0x8005df90 and the method at +0x150 are not named.
Whether the 32 copied bytes are stats, a transform, or both is inferred from the destination offset, not from a field table.

template.summary: Per-frame update of the battle banner/message. Opens a scratch context (F0x8001f648), sets text 0x1005 through a display callback, advances a 0..4 cycle counter at +0x90 and a frame timer at +0x94, and draws the banner with text ids 0x286/0x455 and 0x31/0xb at screen depth 0xd0/0xbc, width 0x140. A player sees the battle's banner text and its cycling animation refresh each frame.
unknowns: The display callbacks come from a scratch struct filled by F0x8001f648; their identities are not established.
The text ids 0x286, 0x455, 0x31 and 0xb are not resolved to strings here.

template.signature: void battleMemberActionAssign(int32_t member, int32_t slot, int32_t action)
template.summary: Records a chosen action for a battle party member. Calls F0x8009bc94 and F0x8009bda4 to resolve the member and action, writes the action into the per-member table at D0x800a3868 (stride 0x1c) or, for an out-of-range member, into the pending-action block at D0x800a4780, then sets bit 0x2 of the member's action-state byte at +0x1c. A player sees the action they picked for a Digimon registered for the round.
unknowns: F0x8009bc94 and F0x8009bda4 are unnamed helpers.
The action-state bit field at +0x1c is treated per this routine; its full enumeration is unknown.

template.summary: Reads the battle roster's active-member byte (D0x800a43f4+0x20) and slot (D0x800a43f4+0x24), looks up the member's sprite/actor slot through D0x800a4580's method at +0xa8, resolves the member's stat byte (D0x80042bca+slot*0x12) and writes a status value into the battle state byte D0x800a442f. A player sees the active member's status marker on the battle HUD update.
unknowns: The method at D0x800a4580+0xa8 and the status byte at D0x800a442f are not named elsewhere.
The exact HUD element the status byte drives is not established.

template.summary: Returns base + the stat byte of the party member named by the roster index at D0x800a43f4+0x24 (member table D0x80042bca, stride 0x12, stat at +0xa). A player-facing lookup into the active party's per-member stat table.
unknowns: The roster index at D0x800a43f4+0x24 is assumed to be the active member; not confirmed at the call sites.

template.summary: Rolls the random source (D0x8005dbf4) masked to 0x7f and returns whether it falls below the party member's stat byte (D0x80042bca+index*0x12+0xb). A statistic-driven random check used by the battle system.
unknowns: Which battle decision this check gates is not established from this body alone.

template.summary: Data-variant sibling of createUnregisteredObject_thunk_fieldstg_80088a4c: allocates an object from a stage pool through F0x80014504 (fieldstg's twin uses pool 0x80098888/size 0x68; this pair uses pools 0x8008cb70 size 0x80 and 0x80091534 size 0x74) and stores the argument at +0x50. The gapped (type-3) match to the fieldstg twin is by body shape, not a word-identical copy; the pool and record size differ. A player sees an extra object spawned into a stage without being registered in the object list.
unknowns: Gapped match, not gap-0: the member bodies differ from the named twin by pool, size and element-count arguments.
The object types built by the two members are not identified.

template.summary: Per-frame forward for a field/title object: reads the object's state word at +0x10, and if it equals 0x4f calls the object's method pointer at +0x2c with argument 0x50. A player sees an object advance its animation/behaviour only while it is in state 0x4f.
unknowns: The state value 0x4f and the constant 0x50 handed to the method are not resolved to named states.
The family spans fieldstg and stdwtitl; only the fieldstg member is in this pass's read.

template.summary: Data-variant sibling of createInnRestScreen: allocates 0x390 bytes from the stage pool at 0x800959b0 through F0x80014504, stores the argument at +0x50 and a sentinel -1 into the argument's first word. The gapped (type-3) match to createInnRestScreen is by body shape only; the pool, the size (0x390 vs 0xa0) and the trailing store differ. A player sees a large screen/panel object built at a stage transition.

exe/fns:F0x8001104c.name: restoreActiveParty
exe/fns:F0x8001104c.summary: Walks the three party positions, resolves each to a live roster record, and restores it to fighting condition: current HP is set back to max (+0x20 from +0x22), current MP likewise (+0x24 from +0x26), and a short run of halfwords near the front of the record is zeroed - the temporary battle state. This is the full-heal-and-clear applied to the whole active party.

exe/fns:F0x80013c30.name: acquireCacheSlot
exe/fns:F0x80013c30.summary: Keyed 64-entry by-16-byte slot cache at D0x80044b3c. On a hit it touches the entry's +0x8 with the current frame tick (the 0x8004de10+0x188 counter) as an LRU keep-alive; on a miss it claims a free slot, records the key, computes a load parameter, marks the slot active and raises the global dirty flag D0x80044b38.
unknowns: What the cache holds is NOT established (texture page, sound, or effect slot are all consistent). Needs the identity of the loader D0x8004b5f4 and of F0x80014200 via D0x80048744, plus a caller trace showing the key domain.

exe/fns:F0x80013e5c.name: resourceGetBase
exe/fns:F0x80013e5c.summary: Returns the RAM base of a resource file, loading it from disc synchronously if not resident and stamping its last-use frame tick. The 64-entry, 0x10-byte cache at D0x80044b3c holds state at +0x00 (3 = resident), fileId at +0x04, LRU tick at +0x08 and the data base at +0x0c. The blocking miss path is the mechanism behind the game's loading pauses on stage transitions.
unknowns: Only state 3 is discriminated; the full +0x00 state enumeration is unknown.
Calling the miss path specifically a DISC load is not traced to a CD command.
Behaviour when all 64 slots are full is not visible in this function.

exe/fns:F0x800140d8.name: packGetEntry
exe/fns:F0x800140d8.summary: Resolves one member of a packed archive: takes the high half of the handle as a resource file id, gets that file's base via resourceGetBase, reads the 32-bit relative offset at base[entryIndex] and returns base + offset. This is the plumbing behind every sprite sheet, map chunk, portrait and UI atlas.
unknowns: The function performs NO range check on entryIndex; whether a bound lives in the header is not visible here.

exe/fns:F0x800143dc.summary: Allocates an object and optional separate extra-state buffer, installs the shared eight-method state-machine block at +0x28..+0x44, and registers it only when registryKey is nonzero.

exe/fns:F0x80014854.name: saveManagerInit
exe/fns:F0x80014854.summary: Initialises the memory-card save manager at D0x80048750: cardSystemInit F0x8003b56c(0), cardManagerInit F0x8003bdc8, a 0x328-byte clear through the D0x8004b600 helper, +0x9C = 3, +0x314 = -1, selectSaveSerial F0x800148c0, then +0x310 = 0x100 and +0x30C = 0x2700. exe/fns:F0x800148c0.name: selectSaveSerial
exe/fns:F0x800148c0.summary: Picks the memory-card save-file name for the console's region from the id at D0x8005cca8: ids 0..6 index the 7-entry table at D0x80010114 (0 selects BISLPS-03446DMW3-JPN, 1 selects BASLUS-01436DMW3-USA, 2..6 select BESLES-03936DMW3-EUR, and any id >= 7 falls through to the Japan case); the selected stub stores the string pointer at D0x8004875c. exe/fns:F0x800148f4.summary: Stores the Japan save serial BISLPS-03446DMW3-JPN (D0x800100cc) at D0x8004875c.

exe/fns:F0x80014930.signature: void saveBuildHeader(s32 name, s32 unused, s32 count, s32 *words)
exe/fns:F0x80014930.summary: Builds the 0x80-byte save-card header at D0x80048750+0x10 when count is 1..3 and F0x8002525c() < 0x41: stores count at +0x314, zeroes the header, writes the 'S','C' magic at +0x10/+0x11, version 4 at +0x13 and (count|0x10) at +0x12, copies the name argument into +0x14 through F0x8002518c, fills the unaligned word fields +0x73..+0x8F, then copies count words from the array argument into +0x318. Body read at fns.s L5019 onward; the unaligned fields are unresolved in the lifted C.

exe/fns:F0x80014aa8.name: cardManagerPoll
exe/fns:F0x80014aa8.summary: Polls the memory-card manager's in-flight operation via cardEventPoll(1,&event,&result) and latches event->D0x80048750+0x90, result->+0x94; results 2 or >=4 are held for up to +0x9C(3) polls with reissue flag +0xA0 set; returns 1 when accepted, 0 while pending.

exe/fns:F0x80015108.name: stgmcardSaveChunkLoop
exe/fns:F0x80015108.summary: Case-4 arm of the memory-card chunked-save engine F0x80014fc4 and host of the common 0x80-byte sector loop all five cases jump into at .L0x80015134: computes the card byte offset manager+0x304 = (manager+0x314 << 7) + (manager+0x310 + 0x80) + (manager+0x30C << 1), then loops the card-write queue start F0x8003cdc4(slot<<4, manager+0xC, buffer, offset, 0x80) pumping the card poll F0x80014aa8; a nonzero queue result stores state 4 at D0x80048750+0 and returns 0, and the state==4 resumption at 0x80015184 advances manager+0x300 in 0x80-byte sectors until the caller's total size, clears state and returns 1. A jump-table case body, not a standalone routine: cases 0-3 end with `j .L0x80015134` into this section and the epilogue at 0x80015264 is shared with F0x80014fc4.

exe/fns:F0x80015590.name: getFlagBit
exe/fns:F0x80015590.signature: int32_t getFlagBit(uint8_t *bankBase, int32_t bitIndex, int32_t expected)
exe/fns:F0x80015590.summary: Stored-bank flag reader and the exact twin of setFlagBit: it tests bit 1<<(bitIndex&7) of bankBase[bitIndex>>3] and returns whether the bit matches the caller's expected polarity. Every stored-bank predicate in the game bottoms out here.

exe/fns:F0x800155d4.name: setFlagBit
exe/fns:F0x800155d4.signature: void setFlagBit(uint8_t *bankBase, int32_t bitIndex, int32_t value)
exe/fns:F0x800155d4.summary: Stored-bank flag setter: indexes bankBase by bitIndex>>3 and sets or clears bit 1<<(bitIndex&7) depending on whether value is non-zero. The write twin of the getter F0x80015590; the bank dispatcher F0x800165ac routes bank 0 here against D0x80048abc and bank 0x1c against D0x8004b3b5.

exe/fns:F0x8001561c.name: bank70CompoundFlagTest
exe/fns:F0x8001561c.summary: The opcode-0x00 leaf: a set of hand-written compound conditions over the save block at D0x80048d34. Each selector ANDs several independent 'this happened OR that happened' pairs and then applies a final either/or, i.e. it answers a multi-part story question such as whether every prerequisite of a chapter gate is satisfied. It reads state only and never writes.
unknowns: Which story gate each selector case corresponds to is not identified; the individual save-block offsets it reads are unnamed.

exe/fns:F0x80015754.name: bank70RosterTest
exe/fns:F0x80015754.summary: The opcode-0x10 leaf and the largest of the family: a wide switch of roster and partner questions answered against DIGIMON_CUR_STATS and the per-partner records at D0x80048d34 (stride 0x3dc). Selector 0 compares the argument against DIGIMON_CUR_STATS+0x1ed8; selector 1 reads the partner record's +0x760. These are the predicates behind 'do you have this Digimon' and 'is this partner in this state' checks.
unknowns: Only selectors 0 and 1 were read; the remaining switch cases and the meaning of +0x760 are unresolved.

exe/fns:F0x80015aac.name: bank70Currency
exe/fns:F0x80015aac.signature: int32_t grantCurrency(int32_t selector, uint8_t payload, uint8_t *entry, int32_t mode)
exe/fns:F0x80015aac.summary: The opcode-0x20 currency leaf. Sub-selector 1 ADDS addTable[param] (D0x80048c6c) to the player's BIT total at D0x80048da0, capped at 9,999,999; sub-selector 0 is the read-only test BIT >= compareTable[param] (D0x80048c44); sub-selector 2 SUBTRACTS subtractTable[param] (D0x80048c8c), floored at 0. This is the single path by which a search point or an on-close script hands the player money.
unknowns: 20 of the 28 currency sub-selector/param combinations have no individually traced use site.

exe/fns:F0x80015b9c.name: bank70RangeTest
exe/fns:F0x80015b9c.summary: The opcode-0x30 leaf: a band test. It reads a two-byte {low, high} row from the range table at D0x80048cb4 and returns whether DIGIMON_CUR_STATS+0x1ed4 falls inside that inclusive band. This is how a script asks 'is the player's progress between these two points' rather than testing a single flag.
unknowns: The quantity held at DIGIMON_CUR_STATS+0x1ed4 is read as the progress ordinal by position in the roster-predicate extraction; it was not independently re-derived here.

exe/fns:F0x80015bd8.name: bank70CollectionCount
exe/fns:F0x80015bd8.summary: The opcode-0x40 leaf: a counting predicate. Selector 0 walks bits 0x27 through 0x2d of the bank at D0x8004b3b5 through getFlagBit, tallying how many are set and how many are clear, then answers one of several questions about that tally depending on mode - all of them set, none of them set, or the raw count. This is the shape of a 'have you collected them all yet' check.
unknowns: What the 7 bits at 0x27..0x2d of bank D0x8004b3b5 collect is not identified, and only selector 0 of the switch was read.

exe/fns:F0x80015d4c.name: bank70TriggerSceneObject
exe/fns:F0x80015d4c.summary: The opcode-0x50 leaf, and the only member of the family that is purely an ACTION rather than a question. It looks up the scene object of type 0x16 through the resident type lookup at D0x8004b7bc and calls that object's +0x2c state method with state 3, then always reports success. In player terms this is the table entry that makes something in the room react.
unknowns: Which scene object class type 0x16 is, and what its state 3 does, are not identified.

exe/fns:F0x80015d90.name: dispatchBank70Entry
exe/fns:F0x80015d90.summary: The bank-0x70 entry dispatcher. It linearly scans the 120-entry, 3-byte-per-record table at D0x80048ad8 ({key, op, param}) for a matching key, stopping at the 0xFF terminator, then calls OP_HANDLER[op & 0xf0](op & 0x0f, param). The SAME table serves both directions: read through get_flag it answers a question about the player's state, written through set_flag it performs a reward or action. Handlers by opcode: 0x00 F0x8001561c, 0x10 F0x80015754, 0x20 F0x80015aac (currency), 0x30 F0x80015b9c, 0x40 F0x80015bd8, 0x50 F0x80015d4c.
unknowns: Only 8 of the 28 currency sub-selectors under opcode 0x20 have a traced meaning.

exe/fns:F0x80015fbc.name: partyCharismaThreshold
exe/fns:F0x80015fbc.summary: The bank-0x72 virtual predicate: it walks party positions 0-2 through the roster-slot lookup at save+0x2718, skips undeployed members, builds each one's effective stats through save+0x2734 and sums their Charisma, then compares the party total against the 15-entry threshold table at D0x80048cf8 (60, 150, 210, 285, 378, 492, 630, 795, 990, 1218, 1482, 1785, 2049, 2277, 2472). Bank 0x72 has no write arm at all, so party Charisma is always recomputed and never stored. In play this is the check behind boarding the El Dorado, the ElDoradoID grant in Asuka City, and Yellow Cruiser tamers refusing a card battle when the party is not charismatic enough.
unknowns: The per-member modifier table at D0x80042b98 keyed by record +0x3c0 is undecoded, so whether equipment can raise summed Charisma is unproven.
The threshold table is anchored to a RAM dump rather than to data.rs.

exe/fns:F0x800160a8.name: getRouteHalfPredicate
exe/fns:F0x800160a8.summary: The bank 0x7E virtual predicate: it stores no bits of its own but compares the caller's index against one of two u16 route cursors. Indices below 0x1E test D0x80048d78 against index+1; the rest test D0x80048d7a against index-0x1D. So bank 0x7E splits one predicate space into two route halves, each answering 'is this the route currently selected'. Polarity selects whether a match reads as true or false.

exe/fns:F0x800161d8.name: adjustItemCount
exe/fns:F0x800161d8.summary: The one place an item's held count changes. The count is a single byte at D0x80048d34 + 0x7c + index - the same array that carries the FishingPole and TreeBoots possession bytes - and every one of banks 0x80 through 0x8e routes here, so the bank never selects a different array, only the index does. Adding past 99 increments and then re-clamps to 99, silently: there is no rejection and no 'inventory full' message, the extra copy simply evaporates. Removing from a stack already at 0 floors at 0 rather than wrapping negative.
unknowns: A side branch taken when removing an item already at count 0 loops the three party slots and calls the equip helper; it FAILS m2c decompilation and is untraced. It resembles an auto-unequip-on-depletion path, but that is a guess and is not asserted.

exe/fns:F0x80016314.name: consumeCollectionC
exe/fns:F0x80016314.summary: The bank-0x92 arm. With a non-zero second argument it launches a UI through the resident pointer D0x8004b454; otherwise it DECREMENTS by one the byte at save+0x3a2+index - collection array C - and, if that underflows below zero, snaps it back to 0 rather than wrapping to 255. So bank 0x92 is where a countable collectible is spent.
unknowns: Which UI D0x8004b454 launches is not identified.

exe/fns:F0x800163b0.name: getFlag
exe/fns:F0x800163b0.summary: The single dispatcher every story, field-script and gate flag check routes through. Splits the id into a bank ((id>>8)&0xfe) and a bit index (id&0x1ff), then either bit-tests the selected byte array for a stored bank or calls a bank-specific predicate for a virtual bank. This is what answers 'has the player collected X / talked to Y / passed story beat Z'.
unknowns: Five of the six virtual-bank predicates were not opened: F0x80015ec8, F0x80015d90, F0x800160a8, F0x80015f04, F0x80015f70. Only the bank-0x72 predicate F0x80015fbc is cross-checked against prior work.

exe/fns:F0x800165ac.name: setGameState
exe/fns:F0x800165ac.summary: The universal persistent-state write opcode and the exact write counterpart of getFlag: same packing, bank = (id>>8)&0xfffe and index = id&0x1ff. Storage banks flip a bit in a byte array; action banks add a roster member, change an item count (bank 0x80+, +1 clamped at 99 or -1 clamped at 0), or launch a screen. This is behind essentially every persistent consequence of a player action: a chest granting an item, a flag that changes an NPC's dialogue, a Digimon joining the party.
unknowns: Bank 0x60 (the progress ordinal) has NO branch in this function, so it is written elsewhere. This is a negative from reading the complete body and contradicts a naive 'all banks go through set_flag' reading.
Banks 0x12/0x14/0x16 have no branch and are silently no-ops.
The handlers for banks 0x90/0x92/0x94/0x7a/0x7c call overlay-resident code and were not traced.

exe/fns:F0x80016924.name: evaluateFlagConditions
exe/fns:F0x80016924.summary: Returns 1 only if every {flagId, expected} pair in a 0xffff-terminated list matches getFlag. This is the AND-of-getFlag twin of applyFlagList, and it gates both whether an NPC is present on a map at all and which line of dialogue that NPC gives you.
unknowns: No ledger claim cites this address; support is research-document grade, though it is load-bearing in the build (it drives tools/wstag_extract.py spawn_flags for 2472 of 2578 scene NPCs).

exe/fns:F0x80016988.name: applyFlagList
exe/fns:F0x80016988.summary: Walks a 0xffff-terminated list of {uint16 id, uint16 value} pairs and calls setGameState on each. This is the batch behind every moment where talking to an NPC sets several flags at once, such as a quest completing together with an item grant.
unknowns: No ledger claim cites this address; the support is research-document grade, not a ledgered claim.
The caller census is not exhaustive: a single genuine call site was located.

exe/fns:F0x80016b28.name: commitScreenTransition
exe/fns:F0x80016b28.summary: Commits a requested screen change: it moves the pending selector at save+0x26c8 into current at +0x26c4, clears pending, and saves what was current into +0x26cc as the previous selector. That saved previous value is what lets a screen know where the player came from.
unknowns: Reached only through the resident-service pointer table D0x8004b434, never by a jal, so its callers cannot be enumerated statically.

exe/fns:F0x80016b78.name: getCurrentShopId
exe/fns:F0x80016b78.summary: Plain getter for the global D0x8004b404, identified by prior research as the current shop id used when a shop screen is entered.
unknowns: The doc that names D0x8004b404 as shop_id also flags the hop that writes it as 'structural, not statically' resolved, so the WRITER of this global is not established here.

exe/fns:F0x80016b88.name: requestScreenTransition
exe/fns:F0x80016b88.summary: Requests the next screen. It is the ONLY writer of both the pending selector at save+0x26c8 (D0x8004b3fc) and the param slot at +0x26d0 (D0x8004b404); F0x80016b28 later commits pending into current at +0x26c4, clears pending, and saves the previous selector to +0x26cc. The param slot is the same one the shop UI reads back as the live shop id, so 'which shop you walked into' and 'which screen to open' travel together through this one call.
unknowns: Neither this function nor its committer is reached by any jal in the corpus - both are called through the runtime resident-service pointer table - so the specific caller identified for the gym path is inference from 'only writer' plus a live capture, NOT a read instruction.

exe/fns:F0x80016d94.name: partyPositionToRosterSlot
exe/fns:F0x80016d94.summary: Bounds-checked accessor: for partyPosition < 3 returns the word at D0x80048d34 + 0x70 + 4*pos (the roster slot for that active-party position); otherwise returns -1. The -1 is produced in the jr delay slot.
unknowns: The three-slot bound is the active party size; whether any caller passes an out-of-range value deliberately as an 'is there a third partner' probe is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80016fd8.name: getFollowerRosterSlot
exe/fns:F0x80016fd8.summary: Returns a follower's fixed roster-slot ordinal, 0-7. This matters more than it looks: it is the value plumbed into the field-entity constructor's kind argument for a party follower, so a follower's kind is always 3..10 and can never reach the six-value shadow denylist. Every party member keeps its drop shadow no matter what it digivolves into - the denylist is reachable only through the NPC id path.

exe/fns:F0x800170c8.name: setLiveStat
exe/fns:F0x800170c8.signature: void setLiveStat(int32_t slot, int32_t statIndex, int32_t value)
exe/fns:F0x800170c8.summary: Clamped writer for the 19 live halfword stat fields at DIGIMON_CUR_STATS[slot] + 0x1c. It computes the record address from the roster slot, selects one halfword by index, and clamps the stored value.
unknowns: The checked-in EXE assembly shows no symbolic jal callsite, so its callers are unidentified; the clamp bound was not re-read here.

exe/fns:F0x80017174.name: buildEffectiveStats
exe/fns:F0x80017174.summary: The per-turn effective-stat builder: it projects persistent buffs over the base stats for the six combatants, and is reached through battle context +0x2734. NOT the DV-Plug or item-use applier - that reading is recorded as falsified.
unknowns: exe-decomp/c/F0x80017174.c is EMPTY - m2c produced no body, so this entry rests on research prose plus the battle-context slot, not on lifted code.

exe/fns:F0x80017578.name: addPersistentBuff
exe/fns:F0x80017578.signature: void addPersistentBuff(EffectiveStats *stats, int32_t which, int32_t amount)
exe/fns:F0x80017578.summary: Adds a persistent buff into the effective-stat buffer, with every stat capped at 999. Selector 7 is the broad case - it adds the same amount to all six stats in the first group - while selectors 1-6 and 8-14 each hit one stat in one of two halfword groups. The 999 ceiling is why stacking boosts stops mattering past that point.
unknowns: Which stat each selector index names is not established; only the grouping and the cap were read.

exe/fns:F0x800176ac.name: validateEquippedForm
exe/fns:F0x800176ac.summary: Validates the three equipped digivolution slots of a roster member: a slot passes only when it is empty (id below 3) or the id resolves inside that same owner's 44-entry form ledger. This is the DRI-side source check - you cannot equip a form the partner has never acquired - and it is distinct from the battle-side check, which validates the live current form index within that same equipped set.
unknowns: The form-ledger entry's acquisition byte at +0x03 has meaning beyond mere presence that is unresolved.

exe/fns:F0x80017a1c.name: readFormLedgerEntry
exe/fns:F0x80017a1c.signature: void readFormLedgerEntry(int32_t owner, int32_t formIndex, void *out)
exe/fns:F0x80017a1c.summary: Reads exactly five words for one owner/form pair out of the acquired-form ledger. Each roster slot owns 44 entries of 0x14 bytes holding the form id, form level, DVEXP and six flagged technique halfwords - so this is the read behind everything the DRI screens show about a form.

exe/fns:F0x80017b70.name: listUnlink
exe/fns:F0x80017b70.summary: Detaches a node from a doubly-linked list: takes the record base at node-0xc, clears the marker at +0x8, and conditionally relinks each neighbour, guarded by a not-sentinel check on both sides.
unknowns: WHICH list this detaches from is NOT established; no caller was resolved. The object-registry guess is a lead only, with no call edge found linking it to the objectSetPhase/createUnregisteredObject family.

exe/fns:F0x80017cb0.name: zeroFill
exe/fns:F0x80017cb0.summary: Generic memory clear: byte-wise when length is not a multiple of 4, word-stride when it is.
unknowns: m2c renders the aligned branch as a byte store through an s8* advanced by 4, which is very likely a misrendered word store. The zeroing effect is unaffected; confirming the true store width needs the paired _asm listing.

exe/fns:F0x80018854.summary: Reads the halfword at +0x48 of pad record padIndex in the input block D0x8004b7d0. Record stride is 0x1c0 (448) bytes, computed as (padIndex*8 - padIndex) << 6.

exe/fns:F0x80018980.signature: unsigned char getPadRecordByte0xa4Indexed(int padIndex, int byteIndex)
exe/fns:F0x80018980.summary: Reads the byte at +0xa4 + byteIndex of pad record padIndex in D0x8004b7d0, same 0x1c0 stride as getPadRecordHalfword0x48. Takes a second sub-index argument that its sibling does not, so +0xa4 is the base of a byte array inside each pad record.

exe/fns:F0x80023738.summary: Advances one controller transaction per frame: reads the stage index at D0x80055db4, calls the stage function from the five-entry table D0x80055df8 with the pad block, and pre-increments the index. exe/fns:F0x80023d80.summary: Stores a controller command in a pad block: +0x37 = command byte, +0x2C = payload pointer, +0x36 = payload length.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008400c.summary: Skips ahead in the effect script when that side still has cards left in the deck.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008404c.name: effectOp_10_branchIfFieldUnderSix
pro/cardgame:F0x8008404c.summary: Skips ahead in the effect script when that side has fewer than six Digimon on the board.

pro/cardgame:F0x80084090.name: pollEffectTimer
pro/cardgame:F0x80084090.summary: Ticks the current effect's countdown by elapsed time and reports whether the wait has run out.

pro/cardgame:F0x800840d0.name: effectOp_4b_pickSelectionBySide
pro/cardgame:F0x800840d0.summary: Picks which card the step will act on: one stored index for side 0, a different stored index for side 1.

pro/cardgame:F0x800840f0.name: markSlotsMatchingEffectAttr
pro/cardgame:F0x800840f0.summary: Marks every board slot whose extra attribute matches the card being resolved, so the next step knows which Digimon the effect may hit.

pro/cardgame:F0x80084188.name: aiPickBestOppFieldSlot
pro/cardgame:F0x80084188.summary: The opponent AI scores each of the six far-side board slots, keeps only the best one marked, and records it as the chosen target.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008423c.name: playSEnergyFlourish
pro/cardgame:F0x8008423c.summary: Turns the S-Energy effect steps into one of five on-screen flourishes, aimed at your side or the opponent's, then plays that flourish.

pro/cardgame:F0x80084320.name: runEffectOpcode
pro/cardgame:F0x80084320.summary: Runs one step of a card's effect script: starts the queued command, then advances the command already on screen until it finishes or chains to the next.

pro/cardgame:F0x80085de8.name: sortPickerCardList
pro/cardgame:F0x80085de8.summary: Re-orders the 40-card picker list by the current sort key, then puts the card that was under the cursor back under it.

pro/cardgame:F0x80085f38.name: pickerCardIsLegal
pro/cardgame:F0x80085f38.summary: Looks up the highlighted card and answers whether this picker is allowed to take it — any card in one mode, only a matching type in another.

pro/cardgame:F0x80085fd0.name: pickerRowIsLegal
pro/cardgame:F0x80085fd0.summary: The picker's grey-out test: in one mode it checks the card's energy cost against the remaining pool; otherwise it uses the type-match test.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086090.name: pickerLangLayoutCoord
pro/cardgame:F0x80086090.summary: Reads one picker-box coordinate from a per-language layout table, so the windows sit in the right place in each language build.

pro/cardgame:F0x800860d4.name: pickerOpenSequenceTick
pro/cardgame:F0x800860d4.summary: Runs the picker's opening sequence: a small script table brings in which window, banner and header on which step.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086330.name: effectOp_98_openOwnFieldPicker
pro/cardgame:F0x80086330.summary: Opens the prompt to pick one of your own board cards, or skips to a no-choice close if nothing there is legal.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008642c.name: tickYesNoConfirm
pro/cardgame:F0x8008642c.summary: Runs the yes/no box: left and right move between the two answers with a click, confirm takes the answer, cancel backs out.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086a18.name: pickerDetailPanelClear
pro/cardgame:F0x80086a18.summary: Blanks the picker's detail panel — portrait, element badge, cost and the two description lines.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086a30.name: pickerDetailPanelFill
pro/cardgame:F0x80086a30.summary: Fills the detail panel for the row under the cursor: portrait, element badge, cost, and a description from the card's type (five cards use a different line).

pro/cardgame:F0x80086d28.name: pickerPageToRowOffset
pro/cardgame:F0x80086d28.summary: Turns which third of the list you are in into a row offset of 0, 6 or 12, then refreshes the detail panel.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086d78.name: openLegalRowPicker
pro/cardgame:F0x80086d78.summary: Opens a card list where each row is tested up front, so illegal rows show greyed before you move.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086eb0.name: openBrowsePicker
pro/cardgame:F0x80086eb0.summary: Opens a card list where every row is legal — used when you are only browsing, not choosing under a rule.

pro/cardgame:F0x80086f24.name: pickerCursorMove
pro/cardgame:F0x80086f24.summary: Moves the picker cursor one row: drops the old row, lifts and re-colours the new one, and plays the move click.

pro/cardgame:F0x800870a4.name: pickerCursorMoveFromList
pro/cardgame:F0x800870a4.summary: The same cursor move, but the list length comes from a list object rather than a plain count.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008722c.name: pickerRegreyRows
pro/cardgame:F0x8008722c.summary: Re-greys every picker row after a selection changes, so cards that are now illegal dim immediately.

pro/cardgame:F0x80087308.name: pickerNothingSelectable
pro/cardgame:F0x80087308.summary: Answers whether nothing on this picker is selectable, used to decide whether to offer confirm at all.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008735c.name: spendOrRefundEnergy
pro/cardgame:F0x8008735c.summary: Adds or subtracts the highlighted card's energy cost from that colour's counter and redraws the number.

pro/cardgame:F0x80087458.name: pickerToggleTick
pro/cardgame:F0x80087458.summary: Toggles the tick on the card under the cursor, refusing a seventh pick, and keeps the selected count and the row's tick mark in step.

pro/cardgame:F0x800875ac.name: pickerPadPickOne
pro/cardgame:F0x800875ac.summary: Pad handling for the pick-one list: up/down scroll, confirm takes the row if it is legal, cancel leaves.

pro/cardgame:F0x800878b4.name: pickerPadPickSeveral
pro/cardgame:F0x800878b4.summary: Pad handling for the pick-several list: same scrolling, but confirm toggles a tick instead of closing.

pro/cardgame:F0x80087b80.name: pickerPadBrowse
pro/cardgame:F0x80087b80.summary: Pad handling for the browse-only list: scroll and cancel, no confirm.

pro/cardgame:F0x80087dc8.name: pickerConfirmPulse
pro/cardgame:F0x80087dc8.summary: The small pulse the chosen row does when you confirm — zoom in, hold, zoom out, then report finished.

pro/cardgame:F0x80087edc.name: tickCardPicker
pro/cardgame:F0x80087edc.summary: Drives the card-picker screen: open animation, pad, greying, the detail panel, close animation, and which card was picked.

pro/cardgame:F0x80088f0c.name: effectOp_9e_openScoreScreen
pro/cardgame:F0x80088f0c.summary: Opens the end-of-duel score screen and marks the board dirty so the counts will resync.

pro/cardgame:F0x80088f78.name: tickScoreScreen
pro/cardgame:F0x80088f78.summary: Runs the score screen: the four numbers count up toward their totals, a tick plays while they climb, then it waits for a button.

pro/cardgame:F0x800894e4.name: showPhaseBanner
pro/cardgame:F0x800894e4.summary: Shows one of the phase banners (its own text and sound) from a small table.

pro/cardgame:F0x80089580.name: tickPhaseBanner
pro/cardgame:F0x80089580.summary: Holds the phase banner until it has opened and the player presses confirm or cancel, then closes it.

pro/cardgame:F0x800896f0.name: pickerCursorTwoChoices
pro/cardgame:F0x800896f0.summary: Moves the cursor between two side-by-side choices and re-colours both.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008985c.name: effectOp_a7_startCoinToss
pro/cardgame:F0x8008985c.summary: Flips a coin for who goes first: one random bit, two side panels, and the winner's panel marked.

pro/cardgame:F0x80089974.name: tickCoinToss
pro/cardgame:F0x80089974.summary: Drives the coin-toss screen through its animation and hands control on when it settles.

pro/cardgame:F0x80089ed4.name: compareHandsOpenDuration
pro/cardgame:F0x80089ed4.summary: Works out how long the two-hand comparison opening lasts: eight frames per card in the bigger hand, never shorter than three cards' worth.

pro/cardgame:F0x80089f18.name: compareHandsCursorMove
pro/cardgame:F0x80089f18.summary: Moves the cursor inside a list that has three sections (rows 0–5, 6–11, 12+), dropping and lifting the right row in the right section.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008a068.name: tickTwoHandCompare
pro/cardgame:F0x8008a068.summary: Runs the two-hand comparison: opens, lets you scroll both hands side by side with the detail panel, and closes.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ad48.name: enterTwoHandCompareMode
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ad48.summary: Starts the second two-hand comparison, with a mode that later reports which card you picked.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ad58.summary: Forwards its arguments to F0x80089ed4 and does nothing else.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ad98.summary: Runs the second comparison screen and reports which card you picked (combo/summon choice).

pro/cardgame:F0x8008baa4.name: openPilePicker
pro/cardgame:F0x8008baa4.summary: Opens a choose-from-a-pile prompt. The pile kind picks whose board, discard or deck, and rows the effect cannot take are marked unusable first.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008bc8c.name: movePileCursor
pro/cardgame:F0x8008bc8c.summary: Moves the pile-list cursor one row, re-lifting the rows and playing the move sound.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008be04.name: pilePickerPad
pro/cardgame:F0x8008be04.summary: Pad handling for a pile list: left/right through the pile, confirm only on a legal row.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c044.name: tickPilePicker
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c044.summary: Drives the pile picker: open, input, confirm pulse, close. Taking from the deck puts that card on top and shrinks the deck; taking from the discard re-sorts the pile.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c5f0.name: effectOp_9d_autoPickLegalSummons
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c5f0.summary: Auto-picks legal summon cards off a pile until six are ticked, skipping the AI class that never summons, and adds each card's cost as it goes.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c6e0.name: aiHandPick
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c6e0.summary: The AI's pile/hand pick: a jump table on the prompt kind chooses which count to scan, then it walks marked rows and keeps a choice. Jump-table arms are not separate functions.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c7e8.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_ownHand
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c7e8.summary: Jump-table arm of the AI hand pick: reads the player's hand slot so the AI can throw away or steal from it.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c7f4.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_ownDeck
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c7f4.summary: Jump-table arm of the AI hand pick: reads the player's deck slot.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c800.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_theirHand
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c800.summary: Jump-table arm of the AI hand pick: reads the opponent's hand slot.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c80c.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_ownTrash
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c80c.summary: Jump-table arm of the AI hand pick: reads the player's discard slot.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c818.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_theirTrash
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c818.summary: Jump-table arm of the AI hand pick: reads the opponent's discard slot.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c81c.name: aiHandPick_jr_arm_default
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c81c.summary: Fall-through arm of the AI hand pick jump table: no extra pile load.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c8d8.name: aiPickFirstLegalPileCard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c8d8.summary: The AI takes the first legal marked card scanning forward; if it finds none it scans backwards so it always comes away with something.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008c988.name: aiPickLowestStatPileCard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008c988.summary: The AI's other pile pick: takes the card with the lowest looked-up stat, so it throws away its weakest card.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ca4c.name: openChoosePilePrompt
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ca4c.summary: Opens the choose-a-pile prompt with a bit mask of which piles are allowed, and clears the fifteen slot highlights first.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008cb5c.name: tickChoosePilePrompt
pro/cardgame:F0x8008cb5c.summary: Drives the choose-a-pile prompt. Confirm is refused unless the pile you are on actually has cards; cancel closes it.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ce0c.name: openRespondPrompt
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ce0c.summary: Opens the respond-to-the-pending-effect prompt, showing the card just played.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008cfdc.name: tickRespondPrompt
pro/cardgame:F0x8008cfdc.summary: Drives the respond prompt; on confirm it records which pending effect you chose to answer.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d274.name: markFieldByFilter
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d274.summary: Walks all twelve board slots and marks the ones that pass a filter (own side, opponent, all, or a colour test) so a later effect can hit just those Digimon. Jump-table arms are not separate functions.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d3fc.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d3fc
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d3fc.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot when it sits on the acting side.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d42c.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d42c
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d42c.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot when it sits on the opposing side.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d45c.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d45c
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d45c.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot whose colour is not white.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d480.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d480
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d480.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot whose colour is not blue.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4a4.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d4a4
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4a4.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot that is green.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4bc.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d4bc
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4bc.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot whose colour is not red.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4e0.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d4e0
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4e0.summary: Board-filter arm: marks a live slot that is brown.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4fc.name: cardgame_jr_arm_at_8008d4fc
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d4fc.summary: Board-filter arm: marks every live slot (the always-match selector).

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d594.name: tickMultiSlotHighlight
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d594.summary: Drives a prompt that highlights several of the twelve slots at once, lifting them on open and dropping them on close.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d854.name: bumpColourEnergy
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d854.summary: Adds one to a side's S-Energy of the card's colour, capped at 99, and repaints that number.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008d938.name: animCardLeaveSlot
pro/cardgame:F0x8008d938.summary: Plays the card-leaves-its-slot animation for one slot and reports when it has landed.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008da2c.name: moveCardFromFieldToPile
pro/cardgame:F0x8008da2c.summary: Moves a card out of a field slot into one of two destination piles, then repaints that pile's count.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008db7c.name: animCardLiftScale
pro/cardgame:F0x8008db7c.summary: The other card-leaves animation: the card lifts, scales up and stops.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008dc70.name: moveCardToHandOrBoard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008dc70.summary: Moves a card into the board or the other pile and repaints that count.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ddc0.name: playMarkedSlotFx
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ddc0.summary: Plays one visual effect on every currently highlighted board card, and plays one of two sounds depending on which effect.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008def8.name: queueStatChange
pro/cardgame:F0x8008def8.summary: Applies a packed attack/HP change to every highlighted board card, and can set attack to the negative of another stat instead of adding.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008e08c.name: statRampTick
pro/cardgame:F0x8008e08c.summary: Walks every highlighted card's two visible numbers one step toward their targets, stopping at 99 and never going below zero, and reports when they have all settled.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008e398.name: markEffectFieldTargets
pro/cardgame:F0x8008e398.summary: Marks which of the twelve board cards a pending effect may be used on: own side, opponent's side, or cards matching a looked-up kind.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008e5bc.name: tickHandShuffle
pro/cardgame:F0x8008e5bc.summary: Pairs up the marked cards, swaps their contents, and animates each pair trading places. If nothing is marked it skips to the end.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ec44.name: markZoneByMask
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ec44.summary: Marks every card in one pile — hand, deck or discard — whose type passes a bit mask, so an effect can hit 'all Fire cards in your discard'.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008eec8.name: markFieldByMask
pro/cardgame:F0x8008eec8.summary: Marks board cards on the side or sides the mask names, and records afterwards which sides actually had a match.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f0b4.name: effectOp_49_enterSweepBoardToDiscard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f0b4.summary: Sets up the sweep-the-board-into-the-discard countdown from that side's board and discard counts.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f0f4.name: tickSweepBoardToDiscard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f0f4.summary: Runs the sweep: the board number falls and the discard number rises one per seven frames; then every board card is appended to the discard and the board is emptied.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f2d8.name: enterSEnergyDelta
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f2d8.summary: Sets up a change to one S-Energy counter: how far to move and how long to take.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f2ec.name: tickEnergyCounterAnim
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f2ec.summary: Ticks one colour's energy number up or down one pip at a time, with a click, stopping at 0 and 99.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f560.name: tickZeroAllEnergy
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f560.summary: Ticks all five S-Energy counters on both sides down together until every one is zero.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f750.name: effectOp_41_enterReturnResolvingCard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f750.summary: Starts the step that sends the resolving card back to its pile.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f790.name: tickReturnResolvingCard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f790.summary: The resolving card flies out, lands in its owner's discard, both discard numbers repaint, and the pending-effect slot is cleared.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f948.name: effectOp_2a_requestCardCutIn
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f948.summary: Requests the cut-in portrait for the resolving card.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008f978.name: openZoomedCard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008f978.summary: Opens the big zoomed view of a single card, taken either from the board or from the deck.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008fa9c.name: tickZoomedCardToDiscard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008fa9c.summary: Runs the zoomed card view, and when it closes moves the card to the discard, closing the gap in the deck or board list it came from.

pro/cardgame:F0x8008ff08.name: drawPileCardToBoard
pro/cardgame:F0x8008ff08.summary: Takes the top card of a pile and puts it on the board, choosing the banner from which side it was and whether the board was already occupied.

pro/cardgame:F0x80090058.name: tickPlayCardSequence
pro/cardgame:F0x80090058.summary: The play-a-card sequence: waits for the flight to land, closes the gap in the list it came from, shrinks that pile, and bumps the card's S-Energy colour capped at 99.

pro/cardgame:F0x8009076c.name: effectOp_44_enterShuffleDiscardToDeck
pro/cardgame:F0x8009076c.summary: Sets up the shuffle-the-discard-back-into-the-deck count from that side's discard and remaining deck.

pro/cardgame:F0x800907ac.name: tickShuffleDiscardToDeck
pro/cardgame:F0x800907ac.summary: Discard falls and deck rises one per seven frames, then the discard entries are copied back into the deck list and both counts repaint.

pro/cardgame:F0x80090a6c.name: clearMarksSetQuota
pro/cardgame:F0x80090a6c.summary: Clears every highlight and records how many cards the next step should affect.

pro/cardgame:F0x80090a90.name: markTopNOfPile
pro/cardgame:F0x80090a90.summary: Marks that many cards starting from the top of the pile. If the pile runs out it marks what it can — that is how 'draw three' behaves with only two cards left.

pro/cardgame:F0x80090ba0.name: effectOp_48_moveMarkedToBoard
pro/cardgame:F0x80090ba0.summary: Moves every marked card onto the board, then clears the marks and sets the banner.

pro/cardgame:F0x80090cd8.name: tickMoveMarkedToBoard
pro/cardgame:F0x80090cd8.summary: Advances the move-marked-cards-onto-the-board animation as a ten-state step machine. m2c could not recover the jump table; arms are not separate functions.

pro/cardgame:F0x800915d4.name: tickDiscardMarked
pro/cardgame:F0x800915d4.summary: Walks the twelve slots and, for each marked one, plays the card-leaves animation and moves it, one at a time rather than all at once.

pro/cardgame:F0x8009170c.name: markFieldViewByEffectKind
pro/cardgame:F0x8009170c.summary: Lights the matching board portraits for the effect now resolving, using a jump table on that effect's targeting kind.

pro/cardgame:F0x80091858.name: placeCardOnField
pro/cardgame:F0x80091858.summary: Puts a card into the next free field slot: copies its two numbers, stamps the instance, shows the art and starts the landing.

pro/cardgame:F0x800919fc.name: effectOp_56_returnCardToHand
pro/cardgame:F0x800919fc.summary: Takes a card off the board back into a hand slot, closing the gap in the board list and shrinking the board count.

pro/cardgame:F0x80091c6c.name: tickCardLand3
pro/cardgame:F0x80091c6c.summary: The three-stage landing animation for a placed card (settle, hop, land), reporting when it is finished.

pro/cardgame:F0x80091eb0.name: effectOp_57_copyMarkedCardToSlot
pro/cardgame:F0x80091eb0.summary: The copy effect: finds the marked card, copies its whole slot record into the new slot, then plays the landing.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092198.name: tickCardLand5
pro/cardgame:F0x80092198.summary: A longer five-stage version of the placed-card landing, with a wait before it starts.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092438.name: openResolveWindow
pro/cardgame:F0x80092438.summary: Opens the window where a resolving card is shown in the middle of the screen; a different path is taken when another window is still up.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092638.name: tickResolveSequence
pro/cardgame:F0x80092638.summary: Shows the resolving card, waits for a button or a timeout, slides it onto the resolution stack, lights every card it will affect, and copies its state into the stack slot.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092ba4.name: effectOp_14_clearBothBoards
pro/cardgame:F0x80092ba4.summary: Clears both players' boards and repaints both counts.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092c54.name: dealOpeningHands
pro/cardgame:F0x80092c54.summary: Deals six cards to each side off the top of that side's deck and lays both rows face-down.

pro/cardgame:F0x80092e60.name: tickDealTurnStart
pro/cardgame:F0x80092e60.summary: The deal / turn-start sequence: if a side is short of six cards it refills; the cards land one at a time, flip face-up, bump S-Energy, and lift into position.

pro/cardgame:F0x80093624.name: enterDamageTransfer
pro/cardgame:F0x80093624.summary: Sets up the damage transfer: subtracts the attacker's total from the defender's, floors at zero, and works out how much the bar must drain each frame.

pro/cardgame:F0x80093710.name: tickAttackDrain
pro/cardgame:F0x80093710.summary: Runs the attack: the attacker's cards flip one after another, the attacker's number ticks down, the defender's bar drains, and the defender's cards shake.

pro/cardgame:F0x80093adc.name: enterClearPlayedRow
pro/cardgame:F0x80093adc.summary: Starts clearing the played row, from the last card backwards.

pro/fieldstg:F0x8008c130.name: launchPadController
pro/fieldstg:F0x8008c130.summary: The op-13 launch-pad controller, created after the trigger raises the scene lock. Once its inner sub-state at +0x14 reaches 0 it calls the target object's +0x28 method with state 2 - 'opened' - and plays the TELEPORT cue 0x0004001d. This is the actor behind a pad that fires the player to another point. SHADOW ROLE (added 2026-08-04): this controller is also one of the writers of the field-entity shadow flag. It holds a pointer to the ridden entity at controller+0x50 and, in two of its state-transition branches, clears that entity's shadow with sw $zr, 0x74(entity) -- restoring it from a caller-supplied value in a different branch. In play that means the rider's drop shadow is switched off while the pad has them airborne and switched back on when the ride resolves. It is a second, independent shadow mechanism beyond the constructor default and the move dispatcher.

Being hit also WAKES a sleeping combatant: it clears the Asleep bit in the defender's ailment byte, plays a wake message and clears the matching active-status entry.

pro/stitshop:F0x8008c510.name: equipCompareCategory
pro/stitshop:F0x8008c510.summary: Dispatches on the candidate item's category byte (+0x2, values 1..8) and compares it against the roster's equipped weapon slots (+0x3c4/+0x3c6) or accessory slots (+0x3c8/+0x3ca) using the item's power/level fields, returning a small code 0..5. This backs the shop's better/worse equip-suggestion (pawn) cards.
unknowns: The semantic meaning of each of the six return codes is NOT established.

pro/stitshop:F0x8008c800.name: equipItemToSlot
pro/stitshop:F0x8008c800.signature: void equipItemToSlot(int32_t rosterOffset, int16_t newItemId, int32_t updateCounts)
pro/stitshop:F0x8008c800.summary: Performs an equip swap. A two-handed weapon (item category byte +0x2 == 7) clears BOTH hand slots; an accessory (category 8) clears any conflicting accessory of the same sub-family (+0x3) to enforce family exclusivity. It then equips the new item and, when updateCounts is set, adjusts the owned/carried counts on both the old and new item.
unknowns: The accessory-family exclusivity branch (category 8) is structurally clear but not corroborated by an independent claim.
The meaning of the +0x20f and +0x7c count fields is not established.

pro/wstag212:F0x800a5ef4.name: stageMaterializeActorTick_wstag212
pro/wstag212:F0x800a5ef4.summary: The tick of the Main Lobby's materialize effect actor, the blue download halo the player sees when the three partners first appear. On the run state it claims the three slot-tagged point-sprite records (the tag-1/2/3 records of the stage point table read through 0x80099D90), copies the actor's pad coordinates +0x50/+0x54 into them and y-sorts them with the signed table at 0x800A8178. It then steps the three sprite scripts through the one-shot stepper 0x800a5de4, pointers taken from the 3-entry table at 0x800A816C; a step value of 0x12C blanks that slot and 0xFF retires it. When all three end it clears the records, reinitialises the cursors and returns itself to state 0. The full decode, including the SETANIM command handler (0x800a6148, not a lifted function start) and the per-pad sounds, is docs/research/field/materialize-effect-actor.md.
unknowns: The command handler 0x800a6148 is not a function start in the inventory, so it has no separate annotation.
Which pad each download command targets is in the event scripts, not in this body.

pro/wstag415:F0x800a5fa8.name: stageFallingBoulderTick_wstag415
pro/wstag415:F0x800a5fa8.summary: One falling boulder in the Deeper Crevice ride. On reset it reads its 16-byte spawn record from 0x800a7350 indexed by the object's +4 spawn parameter (start x/y, step, gravity, bounce divisor, sequence pointer) and picks the record's animation through the overlay's stepper. Each tick it integrates x/y in 8.8 fixed point and accelerates downward; where the bounce divisor is non-zero it lands once, reverses and damps the fall, triples the horizontal step and plays packed sound 0x40012; below y 0x245 it despawns. Ten builder wrappers each bind one of the ten spawn records. The player sees rocks fall onto the monorail during the crevice ride.
unknowns: The dispatch route from the stage's effect choreography to the ten spawn wrappers was not located.

pro/wstag415:F0x800a6c8c.summary: The scrolling layer's update (spawned by 0x800a6ec0). Player-facing: the Deeper Crevice's rail/foreground layer slides then coasts to a stop.

pro/wstag735:F0x800a6148.summary: Rectangle-versus-viewport test used by the Ice Dungeon launch-pad tick. The pad calls it with 32x32 at the pad and 32x64 above it, so the disc and the strobe column are only submitted to the display list while visible on screen. Called three times by 0x800a620c.

On mode 1 it runs two layered sprite components off the two 32-byte animator cursors at +0x5c/+0x60 and the two script pointers in the table at 0x800A6B30, through the overlay's three-argument one-shot {value, hold} animator 0x800a6194.
