exe/fns:F0x800197a4.name: drawTextElement
exe/fns:F0x800197a4.summary: The shared text element's draw method. It clears the six 0xC-stride segment records at element+0x3C, sets the baseline element+0xB8 to the negated element+0xBC, walks the segment and glyph records, and for each placed glyph calls the token stepper textTokenStep (F0x8001a48c) through the font hooks D0x8004dca0/D0x8004dca4. Observed in nine captured states, called only from the reveal tick textRevealTick (F0x8001ac14).

exe/fns:F0x8001a48c.name: textTokenStep
exe/fns:F0x8001a48c.summary: The text token stepper: consumes the token type at state+0x16 and advances the element cursor. Type 2 draws the current glyph through the D0x8004dca0/D0x8004dca4 hooks and adds the per-character advance from the D0x8004de04 table; types 0 and 1 place a line/segment row from the font metrics at element+0x50; type 4 sets element+0xC3 and returns 3, the done marker.

exe/fns:F0x8001aa10.name: textNextGlyph
exe/fns:F0x8001aa10.summary: Selects the current text segment: indexes the element+0x5C records of stride 0xC, returns 0x8003 when the segment pointer is null or its read cursor +0x64 has reached the length +0x62, otherwise calls the glyph-metrics hook D0x8004de0c and stores the result in state+0x14/+0x16 before handing control tokens to textTokenStep.

exe/fns:F0x8001ac14.name: textRevealTick
exe/fns:F0x8001ac14.summary: The typewriter reveal tick already read in resident-core-services-2026-08-04: ticks the accumulator element+0xA8 against the delay +0xAA, advances the revealed count +0xA4 toward the total +0x62, reveals instantly when the delay is zero or less, and plays the per-character blip through playSound. The nine-state sweep confirms it executes and calls drawTextElement.

exe/fns:F0x800139fc.name: findCacheSlot
exe/fns:F0x800139fc.summary: Scans the 64-entry, 0x10-byte resource cache at D0x80044b3c from slot 0 and returns the entry whose +0x04 file id equals the argument, or NULL. This is the lookup shared by the cache's poll and load paths; its two sibling scans are the first-empty-slot finder (F0x80013a34) and the eviction selector (F0x80013adc).
unknowns: No state check: a matching id in a non-resident slot is returned like any other. Whether callers can observe that is untraced.

exe/fns:F0x80013a6c.name: pollCacheSlot
exe/fns:F0x80013a6c.summary: Looks up a slot with findCacheSlot. On a hit it stamps the slot's +0x08 with the frame tick (the D0x8004de10+0x188 counter) as an LRU keep-alive and reports readiness: 0 when the slot state +0x00 is 3, otherwise 1. On a miss it starts a load with acquireCacheSlot and returns 1. The function never waits; the caller pumps servicePendingCacheLoads.
unknowns: Only ready states 3/1 are discriminated; the full +0x00 state enumeration is unknown.

exe/fns:F0x80013adc.name: selectCacheEvictionVictim
exe/fns:F0x80013adc.summary: Scans the 64 cache slots and, among those whose owner +0x04 is nonzero and whose state +0x00 is 3, returns the one with the smallest touch tick at +0x08 - the least-recently-touched ready slot. Equal ticks are broken by the secondary comparator reached through D0x80048740+0x04.
unknowns: What the D0x80048740+0x04 comparator ranks (owner id, size, or priority) is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80013cdc.name: servicePendingCacheLoads
exe/fns:F0x80013cdc.summary: Pumps the resource cache when the dirty flag D0x80044b38 is set and the service is not busy (D0x80044b04+0x2c must not return 1). It walks the 64 slots: a slot in state 1 issues its load through D0x80044b04+0x30 and advances to state 2, a slot in state 2 advances to state 3 (resident), and each touched slot's +0x08 is stamped with the frame tick. If no slot advanced, the dirty flag is cleared.
unknowns: The load call's D0x80044b04+0x30 interface is only seen from this caller; its own body is elsewhere.

exe/fns:F0x80013e20.name: loadCacheSlotBlocking
exe/fns:F0x80013e20.summary: Acquires a slot for the file id (acquireCacheSlot) and then services pending loads until pollCacheSlot reports the slot ready. This synchronous wait is the mechanism behind the game's loading pauses on stage transitions.
unknowns: Nothing here bounds the loop; a load that never completes would spin forever. No timeout was found.

exe/fns:F0x8001804c.name: iterateRegisteredObject
exe/fns:F0x8001804c.summary: Cursor-based scan of the 100-entry registered-object table at D0x8004b610. Each pointer is matched against the table's three filter words at +0x190/+0x194/+0x198, compared with object fields +0x00/+0x04/+0x08, with -1 as wildcard. The scan starts at the cursor +0x19c, advances it past the object returned, and returns NULL at the end. findRegisteredObject (F0x8001810c) is the cursor-resetting variant over the same table.
unknowns: What advances or resets the cursor between frames is not established here; the relationship to findRegisteredObject is read from the shared filter fields, not traced.

exe/fns:F0x80017e84.name: blockingRetryAlloc
exe/fns:F0x80017e84.summary: Calls the free-list allocator F0x80017d2c(size, mode) and, while it returns NULL, calls the service callback reached through D0x80044b38+0x408 and retries. Returns the block when one is granted. This is the blocking allocation that yields to the frame callback while waiting.
unknowns: The meaning of the second allocator argument (mode) is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80017f54.name: allocZeroed
exe/fns:F0x80017f54.summary: Blocking-allocates a block of `size` bytes (blockingRetryAlloc) and then zeroes it through the resident bzero F0x80017cb0, returning the zeroed block. This is the general 'allocate a clean buffer' helper.
unknowns: Callers pass the size as the sole surviving argument in the decompiled C; the allocator's mode argument is dropped by m2c, not absent in assembly.

exe/fns:F0x8001fcc0.name: initFetcherTable
exe/fns:F0x8001fcc0.summary: Zeroes the first 0xC bytes of the object (through the bzero at D0x8004b600) and installs the three resource-fetch routines at +0x00/+0x04/+0x08 (F0x8001f744, F0x8001f770, F0x8001fa20), then tail-calls F0x8001f738. It is the constructor half of the packed-resource fetch table.
unknowns: The claim covering this table is BATTLE-Q003-C12, still candidate: which resource kind each of the three fetchers serves is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80019370.name: widgetSetLineString
exe/fns:F0x80019370.summary: Installs a string into one of the text widget's embedded line buffers. It measures the string with the resident strlen (F0x8002525c), frees the buffer only when the new text needs more room (D0x8004b5ec), allocates a rounded size through D0x8004b5f4, copies the bytes with F0x8002514c, and sets the widget byte +0xC1 to 1 when text was installed or 0 when the line was emptied. The widget's five line setters (0x800194c4, 0x800195b0, 0x800196e4 and wrappers) all funnel through it; when a setter passes no text it installs the empty literal D0x800101a4.
unknowns: The allocation-size rounding ((len&3)?len+8:len+4) is read from the body but its reason is not established.

exe/fns:F0x800195b0.name: widgetSetLineNumber
exe/fns:F0x800195b0.signature: void widgetSetLineNumber(void *widget, uint32_t line, int32_t value)
exe/fns:F0x800195b0.summary: Sets one of the text widget's six lines from an integer. Line >= 6 is rejected and sets line 0 to the literal D0x800101c8 instead. Otherwise it zero-fills a 16-byte stack buffer, renders the value as decimal ASCII with F0x80019508, converts every emitted digit from ASCII '0'..'9' (0x30..0x39) to the game's own UI digit codes by subtracting 0x2C, installs the buffer through widgetSetLineString, and clears that line's +0x66 halfword. This is the routine behind every number on the shared text widget (money, counts, stats).
unknowns: The 0x2C offset is read from the body and matches the documented font digit encoding; no separate glyph-table check was made here.

exe/fns:F0x80016b9c.name: load_D0x8004b3fc
exe/fns:F0x80016b9c.summary: Bare global getter: returns nonzero when the word at D0x8004b3fc is nonzero. It sits in a run of identically shaped per-global accessors covering D0x8004b3f8, D0x8004b3fc, D0x8004b400 and D0x8004b404, one of which the original assembly already names load_D0x8004b3f8; this name follows that convention. What the word holds is not established.
unknowns: The meaning of D0x8004b3fc is not established; only which word the accessor returns is.

exe/fns:F0x8001d8cc.name: setDisplayRegion
exe/fns:F0x8001d8cc.signature: void setDisplayRegion(int32_t width, int32_t height, int32_t primary, int32_t secondary)
exe/fns:F0x8001d8cc.summary: Branches on its 3rd and 4th arguments to configure one of the display service's region rectangles through F0x8002906c (base inside D0x8004de10), always finishing with one more region call after the branches merge; the first two arguments are the rectangle's width and height. When both flags are set it also raises the clip flags at +0x48/+0x49 and +0x5c/+0x5d. This is the routine that puts up the 320x240 drawing area.
unknowns: Which branch corresponds to which player screen is not established; only the rectangle arithmetic and the flag writes.

exe/fns:F0x8001dbe0.name: registerDisplayView
exe/fns:F0x8001dbe0.summary: Claims a free cell of the 30-cell display-view registry (F0x8001dad0), builds a view from the descriptor through F0x8001e5bc, stores the caller's key verbatim at view+0xD8, and returns the view pointer; returns 0 when every cell is occupied. The key is the exact identity a later view lookup matches on.
unknowns: The view-type/kinds are enumerated from callers (1,2,3,4,8,0xC) but their player meanings are not established here.

exe/fns:F0x8001d714.name: resetDisplayService
exe/fns:F0x8001d714.summary: Init/reset for the display service. On the initialised path it walks all 30 view cells, calls the service destroy callback at D0x8004de10+0x170 for each occupied one, then bzeroes the 0x18-byte registry header. On the first call it instead sets the service's initialised flag and clears the active cursor.
unknowns: Why the destroy callback receives only the key (not the view pointer) is not established.

exe/fns:F0x8002096c.name: touchSeqByArchive
exe/fns:F0x8002096c.summary: Archive-resolved sequencer touch. It resolves which of the three channel records (base D0x800519ec, stride 0x18) holds the archive named by bits 18-24 of the packed word (findAudioChannelByArchive; -1 on miss) and, unless the voice is -1 or no channel holds it, starts the sequence through F0x80034698 with the record's VAB slot at +0x4204 and the packed fields: bits 11-17, bits 7-10 and bits 0-6. A miss is silent - no sound and no error.
unknowns: The exact fields of the packed word (11-17, 7-10, 0-6) are read but their meanings are not established.

exe/fns:F0x80020030.name: findAudioChannelByArchive
exe/fns:F0x80020030.summary: Linearly scans exactly three channel records in the fixed-stride (0x18-byte) array at D0x800519ec, comparing each record's +0x4200 archive id against the argument, and returns the matching channel index 0, 1 or 2, or -1 when none match.
unknowns: Whether a fourth channel exists but is never scanned is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80016b58.name: load_D0x8004b400
exe/fns:F0x80016b58.summary: Bare global getter: returns the word at D0x8004b400. It is one of a run of identically shaped per-global accessors covering D0x8004b3f8, D0x8004b3fc, D0x8004b400 and D0x8004b404; the name follows the original assembly's load_D0x8004b3f8 convention for the sibling. What the word holds is not established.
unknowns: The meaning of D0x8004b400 is not established; only which word the accessor returns is.

exe/fns:F0x80018310.name: resetPadService
exe/fns:F0x80018310.summary: Clears the 0x3E0-byte controller-input service object at D0x8004b7d0, fills 12 bytes at +0x3C8 with 0xFF, and runs a 2-port x 4-slot nested loop calling the keymap-defaults filler F0x800188c0 once per channel. It then initialises the two device buffers at D0x8004b7d4 (34 bytes apart) either as one or as two, stores the channel id at +0x3D4 (defaulting to 0x10 when zero), raises bit 0x40000000 and calls F0x80018460. This is the pad subsystem's cold init.
unknowns: What raises the 0x40000000 bit and who consumes it is not established.

exe/fns:F0x800186e0.name: setPadVibration
exe/fns:F0x800186e0.signature: int32_t setPadVibration(int32_t channel, int32_t motor, int16_t strength, int8_t step)
exe/fns:F0x800186e0.summary: The vibration motor command path, gated by the service capability bit 0x08000000 and a present channel. Controller types 4 and 7 take a special branch; otherwise it sets motor byte +0x3C8 to 0x40 and enables +0x3C9. It stores the strength at the record's +0x6C (or clears it when strength is zero) and submits a two-byte pad command through F0x80020d8c, returning 1 on success and 0 when the gate fails.
unknowns: In the shipped game every syntactic +0x3EC call is in the developer shock-test overlay; no ordinary player screen is known to vibrate the pad.

exe/fns:F0x800188c0.name: initPadKeymap
exe/fns:F0x800188c0.summary: Fills the 16-byte logical-button-to-physical-bit table of one pad record (record +0x5c) from the defaults block at D0x8004bbf4. It is called once per channel by resetPadService. The stored values are bit indices, not masks: the decoder shifts each held button by the table entry.
unknowns: The default table D0x8004bbf4 is applied as-is; its source and whether it is ever authored differently are not established.

exe/fns:F0x80018bcc.name: decodePadRecord
exe/fns:F0x80018bcc.summary: The per-frame input decoder for one channel. It reads the raw pad word through F0x8002116c and maintains the record's button words: +0x06 receives the freshly decoded word, the previous +0x06 is copied to +0x04, +0x00 receives new AND (new XOR previous) - the buttons that went from released to pressed this frame - and +0x02 is cleared then given the repeat bit for held buttons whose timer elapsed. It applies the record's keymap and the pad/multitap presence encoding on the way.
unknowns: The repeat timer's period is read from the record fields but not tabulated here.

exe/fns:F0x8001e5bc.name: initDisplayView
exe/fns:F0x8001e5bc.summary: Allocates a 0x16C-byte display view (through D0x8004b5fc) and fills it from the descriptor: it stores the view type's ordering-table bucket size (halfword table 0x8004dfa0 indexed by type-1: 2,4,8,...,4096) at view+0x64 and allocates the two word arrays at view+0x5c/+0x60 sized from it, then installs the per-type method table. Used by registerDisplayView.
unknowns: The per-type method tables are read by address but their individual draw semantics belong to the display code.

exe/fns:F0x8001f744.name: fetchTableEntry
exe/fns:F0x8001f744.summary: Bounds-gated table fetch: returns NULL when the index is negative or is at least the count stored at table[0], otherwise returns the pointer table plus the 32-bit word offset held at table[index+1]. This is the fetcher installed in the three-entry fetch table by initFetcherTable.
unknowns: What resource kind each of the three fetchers serves is not established.

exe/fns:F0x80018928.name: swapPadKeymapEntry
exe/fns:F0x80018928.signature: void swapPadKeymapEntry(int32_t channel, int32_t entryA, int32_t entryB)
exe/fns:F0x80018928.summary: Exchanges two entries of one pad record's 16-byte logical-button-to-physical-bit table at record +0x5c, addressed by the two byte offsets given. This is the operation a button-configuration screen needs.
unknowns: Which player screen issues the swap is not established from this routine.

exe/fns:F0x8001dad0.name: findDisplayViewCell
exe/fns:F0x8001dad0.summary: Walks the 30-cell display-view registry. With a nonzero key it returns the occupied cell whose key +0xD8 equals the argument; with key 0 it returns the first empty cell. Returns -1 when neither is found.
unknowns: None: the lookup and first-free modes are both read in full.

exe/fns:F0x8001dc7c.name: destroyDisplayView
exe/fns:F0x8001dc7c.summary: Finds a free-targeted view cell, calls the view's own release method at vtable +0x168, frees the view block through D0x8004b5ec, and clears the registry cell with F0x8001db34. Returns 1 when a view was torn down and 0 when no cell matched.
unknowns: The view release method is called by slot, not read here; its body belongs to the display view class.

exe/fns:F0x8001764c.name: findRosterFormEntry
exe/fns:F0x8001764c.summary: Within one roster slot's 44 acquired-form entries (0x14 bytes each, based at D0x80048d34 + slot*0x3DC), scans for an entry whose field +0x7B8 is at least 3 and equals the argument, and returns the entry index or -1. The field is the entry's form level; the full record layout is the roster form entry described by TL-001.
unknowns: The exact halfword at +0x7B8 is called the form level here from the TL-001 layout; a dedicated level test was not made.

exe/fns:F0x800177d0.name: writeEquippedDigivolutions
exe/fns:F0x800177d0.summary: Confirm-path write-back: for each of the three chosen form ids, resolves the roster form entry with findRosterFormEntry and stores the entry index (or -1) into the equipped-digivolutions triple at record+0x50, one halfword per slot. No entry writes 0xFFFF, and the deployed order and current form are untouched.
unknowns: The caller block is untouched by this routine; where the confirm path supplies the three ids is elsewhere.

exe/fns:F0x8001e7ec.name: resolveCardRecord
exe/fns:F0x8001e7ec.summary: Resolves a card's record: with cardId > 0 it stores D0x80044f4c(fileIndex) + ((cardId-1) & 0x3F) * 0x62C into the current-object cell at gp+0x1b8, where fileIndex = (cardId-1)>>6; with cardId 0 it stores D0x80044f4c(D0x8004dfb8).
